nodes.label: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work—Until They Don't
nodes.author: Zhiyuan Jiang et al.
nodes.rationale: Analyzes when and why agent skills improve performance; distinguishes procedural anchoring (65.7%) from knowledge injection (4.5%); studies retrieval, transfer, and failure modes.

nodes.label: Agent Skill
nodes.rationale: Compact procedural abstraction encoding what to do, what to check, and what pitfalls to avoid; differs from raw traces by compressing noisy experience into standardized format; primary mechanism is procedural anchoring (65.7%).

nodes.label: Procedural Anchoring
nodes.rationale: Primary mechanism by which skills improve agent performance (65.7% of cases); stabilizes execution through setup steps, tool sequences, implementation routines, and verification checks rather than injecting factual knowledge.

nodes.label: Workflow Memory
nodes.rationale: Direct procedural memory preserving trace-level execution details; carries irrelevant exploration, failed branches, and process noise; skills improve over workflow memory by 6.06 percentage points in matched comparisons.

nodes.label: Skill Retrieval and Pool Confusability
nodes.rationale: As skill pools grow from 5 to 100, actual-use precision falls from 29.6% to 3.3%; semantic confusability (similar distractors) is more stressful than pool size; exact ground-truth invocation neither sufficient nor necessary for success.

nodes.label: Skill Failure Modes
nodes.rationale: Skills fail under brittle assumptions, incompatible contexts, insufficient adaptation, or when misapplied (10.0% of skill-arm cases); skill_guidance_misapplied_or_ignored appears in 10.0% vs 0.8% for raw execution.

nodes.label: Terminal-Bench
nodes.author: Merrill et al., 2026
nodes.rationale: Realistic command-line task benchmark with isolated environments and test-based verification; 200-task public split from 400-task benchmark spanning 8 domains; used for RQ1-RQ3 controlled experiments.

nodes.label: SkillsBench
nodes.author: Li et al., 2026
nodes.rationale: 86 tasks across 11 domains with native task–skill annotations; designed for skill-based procedural reuse; used for RQ4 retrieval experiments with ground-truth skill labels.

nodes.label: Skill-Use Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: 3 high-level categories (SC1: procedural anchoring, SC2: execution-layer failures, SC3: invocation/boundary failures) and 12 fine-grained modes; derived from 240 sampled trajectories with 95.8% human-LLM agreement (κ=0.952).

nodes.label: Cross-Framework Skill Transfer
nodes.rationale: Skills constructed in Codex framework transfer to Gemini CLI; distilled skills preserve reusable procedural guidance more robustly than direct workflow traces across framework boundaries.

nodes.label: Outcome Annotation in Skill Construction
nodes.rationale: Success/failure labels guide skill construction; impact grows as failed trajectories enter pool; at 3s2f mixture, Gemini skill with labels reaches 0.7462 vs 0.4000 without labels.

nodes.label: Skill Mechanism Labels
nodes.rationale: 5 mechanism categories: procedural_anchor (65.7%), knowledge_injection (4.5%), failure_warning, none, counterproductive; paired trajectory analysis assigns mechanism to each arm to isolate behavior changes.

nodes.label: Skill Execution Bottlenecks
nodes.rationale: Skills reduce environment_infrastructure_failure (5.3%→0.2%), output_format_schema_mismatch (7.4%→3.2%), but do not eliminate algorithmic_logic_error (8.3%) or static_verification (12.5%).

nodes.label: Skill Lifecycle Framework
nodes.rationale: Skills work when prior experience distilled into reusable procedural anchors, retrieved in compatible contexts, and invoked with adaptation; fail when noisy, over-specific, mismatched, or followed rigidly.

nodes.label: A.2 Dive into Skill-Use Mechanisms: Trajectory Labeling and Comparative Analysis
nodes.rationale: Core methodology paper describing trajectory analysis pipeline for comparing agent execution with different prior-experience artifacts

nodes.label: Trajectory Labeling Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage process: open coding → taxonomy induction → paired contrastive labeling → deterministic aggregation

nodes.label: Three Execution Arms
nodes.rationale: Experimental design contrasts baseline (Raw), procedural memory (Workflow Memory), and distilled skills (Skill) to isolate effect of prior-experience representation

nodes.label: Manifest Construction and Trial Normalization
nodes.rationale: Converts heterogeneous benchmark outputs into unified trial table with 8,135 records; aligns injected artifacts with trial outputs; derives success/failure from verifier reward

nodes.label: Open Coding of Individual Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Induces vocabulary from 240 sampled trajectories using Claude Sonnet 4.6 before applying fixed taxonomy; stratified sampling prevents bias toward largest benchmark

nodes.label: Canonical Taxonomy Induction
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Canonical Taxonomy Induction subsection
nodes.rationale: Two-round batched process: batch-level modes (8-14 per batch) → merged into 12 global canonical modes; intentionally mixes success/failure modes to distinguish guidance sources

nodes.label: Paired Contrastive Trajectory Labeling
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Paired Contrastive Trajectory Labeling subsection
nodes.rationale: Central methodological choice: compares raw, workflow, and skill trajectories for same task (528 triples); judges what changed when prior-experience representation changed, not just which modes are frequent

nodes.label: Deterministic Aggregation and Statistical Reporting
nodes.rationale: Final stage computes per-arm success rates, paired deltas with bootstrap CI, mode frequencies, fixed/introduced counts, mechanism distributions without additional LLM calls

nodes.label: React Performance Debugging Example (1s4f setting)
nodes.rationale: Concrete example showing Raw (reward 0, external API bypass), Workflow Memory (reward 0, latency threshold exceeded), Skill (reward 1, all tests pass) for same SkillsBench task

nodes.label: Failure Mode Taxonomy (12 canonical modes)
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Canonical Taxonomy Induction subsection
nodes.rationale: Mixed success/failure modes distinguish when success is attributable to skill guidance, workflow guidance, or autonomous agent behavior

nodes.label: Mechanism Classification
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Paired Contrastive Trajectory Labeling subsection
nodes.rationale: Third level of paired-comparison output: labels mechanism by which skill or workflow affected execution (referenced in Table 2)

nodes.label: Verifier Reward Oracle
nodes.rationale: Positive numeric reward = success; zero/missing/non-positive = failure; keeps taxonomy aligned with benchmark oracle rather than agent self-assessment

nodes.label: Evidence Grounding and Inspectability
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection
nodes.rationale: Evidence quotes make labels inspectable; each mode assignment traceable to trajectory, instruction, result metadata, or skill artifact

nodes.label: Context Budget Management
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Open Coding subsection and Paired Contrastive Trajectory Labeling subsection
nodes.rationale: Fixed budgets for open coding (task 3k, skill 3k, transcript 6k head + 12k tail) and paired labeling (task 3k, skill 3k, each trajectory 4k head + 8k tail) preserve evidence structure while fitting multiple trajectories

nodes.label: Stratified Sampling Strategy
nodes.rationale: Sampler draws from cells defined by benchmark, setting, arm, outcome with minimum examples per cell and fixed seed to prevent dominance by largest benchmark or outcome

nodes.label: Paired Success-Rate Delta Analysis
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap CI (1000 iterations) shows Skill vs Workflow Memory (+0.0606, [+0.0076, +0.1136]) is most robust aggregate difference; skills distill trajectories into more compact actionable form

nodes.label: Representative Trial Selection Policy
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Paired Contrastive Trajectory Labeling subsection
nodes.rationale: Deterministic by default (stable trial-id ordering); seeded random policy supported for sensitivity checks; makes paired label set reproducible

nodes.label: LLM Judge Constraints
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection
nodes.rationale: Strict JSON schemas, evidence quotes, tool use disabled, session persistence disabled, 600-second timeout, caching by trial id to reduce contamination and force judgment on included evidence only

nodes.label: Limitation: Incomplete Token Metrics
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection
nodes.rationale: Some skill-arm token fields incomplete; token cost reported only on matched same-task intersection with complete metadata; mechanism and mode analyses treated as primary evidence

nodes.label: Limitation: LLM-Assisted Rather Than Exhaustively Human-Coded
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection
nodes.rationale: v1 taxonomy induced from 238 valid labels then applied to 528 triples; trajectory grounding and taxonomy aggregation independently human-validated but full paired-triple dataset remains LLM-assisted

nodes.label: Limitation: Representative Trial Policy Does Not Average Repeated Trials
nodes.source_location: Section A.2, Reproducibility and Reliability Controls subsection
nodes.rationale: Selects one trajectory per arm for each task-setting triple; does not average all repeated trials

nodes.label: A Systematic Study of Skill Representation and Transfer in Agent Learning
RQ1: Representation of Prior Experience
nodes.rationale: Compares three conditions (Raw, Workflow Memory, Skill) to isolate whether representing prior experience as direct procedural memory versus distilled skill changes downstream execution performance.

nodes.label: RQ2: Outcome Annotation and No-Hint Ablation
nodes.rationale: Tests whether skill benefits derive from underlying experience content or from explicit success/failure outcome annotations during skill construction.

nodes.label: RQ3: Cross-Framework Transfer
nodes.rationale: Evaluates whether reusable procedural knowledge is tied to the framework that produced it by transferring Codex-derived skills to Gemini framework.

nodes.label: RQ4: Skill Retrieval and Downstream Execution
nodes.rationale: Comprises three independent experiments (embedding-based retrieval, explicit agent selection, real execution) to characterize skill identification and execution on SkillsBench using ground-truth task-skill annotations.

nodes.label: Skill Creator Prompt (Standard)
nodes.rationale: Instructs skill generator to analyze execution traces and produce reusable SKILL.md artifacts with standardized structure including use cases, preconditions, steps, failure modes, and verification.

nodes.label: Skill Creator Prompt (No-Hint Variant)
nodes.rationale: Variant that withholds explicit outcome annotations; skill creator must infer failure patterns only from observable evidence in traces without assuming success/failure labels.

nodes.label: Trajectory Labeling Prompt
nodes.rationale: Instructs labelers to explain why trials ended as they did across raw/workflow/skill conditions, producing structured JSON with mode candidates, evidence spans, and skill effect judgments.

nodes.label: Batch Mode Aggregation Prompt
nodes.rationale: Mines canonical failure/success modes from trajectory labels, producing 8-14 specific procedural patterns covering environment failures, API misuse, debugging loops, verification mismatches, timeouts, and skill-specific patterns.

nodes.label: Taxonomy Merge Prompt
nodes.rationale: Consolidates mode taxonomies from multiple batches into unified 9-14 canonical modes with mappings from batch-level modes to unified targets.

nodes.label: Paired Comparison Prompt
nodes.rationale: Compares 3 agent trajectories on same task across raw/workflow/skill conditions, producing structured analysis of per-arm modes, deltas, and skill/workflow mechanisms.

nodes.label: SkillsBench
nodes.rationale: Benchmark providing native ground-truth task-skill annotations enabling precision/recall/F1 computation without circular dependency on downstream task success.

nodes.label: Workflow Memory Representation
nodes.rationale: Cleaned and structured trajectories preserving procedural flow; serves as baseline for comparing against distilled skill representation.

nodes.label: Skill Representation (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Standardized reusable skill format distilled from workflows; achieves highest success rate (69.6%) while reducing token use relative to raw trajectories.

nodes.label: Arm 1: Embedding-Based Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Offline diagnostic using Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B to rank skills by cosine similarity to task instruction; reports top-1 precision without executing downstream task.

nodes.label: Arm 2: Explicit Agent Selection
nodes.rationale: Agent explicitly chooses skills from available_skills pool without executing task; evaluates whether agent can use task context and skill descriptions to select helpful skills.

nodes.label: Arm 3: Real Execution
nodes.rationale: Complete candidate pool placed in agent's execution environment; measures which skills are actually inspected or invoked during benchmark task execution.

nodes.label: Short-Plan Baseline
nodes.rationale: Lightweight baseline providing concise instruction-derived plan with 3-5 high-level steps; achieves 47.7% success vs 79.2% for Skill on Terminal-Bench-2.

nodes.label: Test-First Template Baseline
nodes.rationale: Workflow-derived validation template emphasizing success conditions, intermediate checks, and final verification; achieves 59.2% success on Terminal-Bench-2.

nodes.label: Skill-Use Taxonomy (SC1/SC2/SC3)
nodes.rationale: Three-level taxonomy: SC1 (successful procedural anchoring), SC2 (execution-layer and verification failures), SC3 (invocation, applicability, and boundary failures); computed over 528 paired triples.

nodes.label: SC1: Successful Procedural Anchoring
nodes.rationale: Includes skill_guided_success (61.6% in Skill condition), workflow_guided_success (54.5% in Workflow condition), and autonomous_clean_success (48.7% in Raw condition).

nodes.label: SC2: Execution-Layer and Verification Failures
nodes.rationale: Includes environment_infrastructure_failure, output_format_schema_mismatch, background_service_lifecycle_failure, shell_code_corruption, algorithmic_logic_error, static_verification_without_runtime.

nodes.label: SC3: Invocation, Applicability, and Boundary Failures
nodes.rationale: Includes timeout_budget_exhaustion, skill_guidance_misapplied_or_ignored, capability_or_safety_limit; captures failures specific to skill invocation and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Matched Token-Cost Analysis
nodes.rationale: Compares token usage on 83-task intersection; Workflow Memory most token-efficient (-129.5K total), Skill achieves highest success (+5.5 pp) while reducing tokens vs Raw (-34.2K total).

nodes.label: Trajectory Pool Construction
nodes.rationale: Balanced pool with sufficient successful and failed runs collected under fixed execution protocol; serves as common source for all Workflow Memory and Skill conditions.

nodes.label: Candidate Pool Construction (RQ4)
nodes.rationale: Each pool contains task's ground-truth skill set plus distractors; pool size varies 5-100; distractors sampled under random, similar (embedding near-neighbors), and dissimilar (far-away) regimes.

nodes.label: Similar Distractor Regime
nodes.rationale: Distractors selected as embedding-space near-neighbors; more challenging than random; top-1 precision drops from 97.7% (random) to 70.5% (similar) for pool size 5.

nodes.label: Dissimilar Distractor Regime
nodes.rationale: Distractors selected from far-away skills; easiest regime; top-1 precision remains high at 96.6% for pool size 5.

nodes.label: Ground-Truth Skill Set (Gt)
nodes.rationale: Set of canonical skill identifiers attached to task by benchmark's native task-skill annotations; not inferred from retrieval outputs or agent success.

nodes.label: Precision, Recall, F1 Computation
nodes.rationale: Skill counts as correct only when canonical identifier occurs in both predicted and gold sets; repeated mentions count once; empty predicted set receives P=R=0.

nodes.label: SKILL.md Format
nodes.rationale: Standardized markdown structure with name, description, use-case conditions, preconditions, ordered steps, common failure modes with mitigations, recovery procedure, and verification criteria.
